newsitem.title: USA: Clintons attend gala at historic Ford's Theater.
newsitem.headline: Clintons attend gala at historic Ford's Theater.

text.p: President Bill Clinton and his wife Hillary spent Sunday evening at a gala at the historic Ford's Theatre in downtown Washington to honour President Abraham Lincoln, who was assassinated there in 1865.
Organisers said the event, also attended by members of Congress, Cabinet secretaries and other administration officials, would raise more than $500,000 for the theatre.
The president had to endure some jokes about the recent fund-raising scandals that have dogged his administration.

Comedian Bill Maher, host of the talk show "Politically Incorrect," said he wouldn't dwell on the investigations into the Democrats' fund raising, but noted "there was a cash bar" at a pre-performance reception at the White House.
"And I hear even Socks is being investigated for meeting with a Siamese cat," he added.
Performers included Natalie Cole, tap-dancer Gregory Hines, singer Jon Bon Jovi, comedian Elayne Boosler and actor Kevin Spacey, who gave a tribute to Lincoln.
The president used the event to recount Lincoln's commitment to the arts, noting that he even found time to visit Ford's Theatre often during the Civil War.
"Over the next four years, I hope all of us can work together to advance the cause of education and strengthen our historic commitment to the arts," Clinton said.
